To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the discount factor plays a crucial role in the learning process of DQNs, and that a dynamic learning rate may be a good alternative to the standard discount factor.

(i) using an increasing discount factor during the learning process can significantly reduce the number and the duration of learning steps, (ii) using a varying discount factor during the training phase can outperform the original DQN, (iii) the learning rate should be increased during the training phase to compensate for the increasing discount factor, (iv) a high discount factor can lead to a local optimum during learning.

(1) using a varying discount factor in a deep Q-learning setting allows to speedup the learning process and improve the performance; and (2) the use of a varying discount factor is a way of dealing with the exploration/expoitation dilemma, which is one of the main challenges in reinforcement learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to use the discount factor in order to reduce the computational complexity of the learning process and to improve the performance of the resulting algorithm.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a dynamic discount factor can be beneficial in a DQN setting and can lead to a significant reduction in the number of learning epochs, especially when the learning rate is also dynamically adjusted.
the use of the discount factor in a DQN is not a trivial choice and that its impact on the quality of the learned policy is non-negligible.
, when using deep reinforcement learning, the discount factor should not be set to a fixed value but rather should be a variable that evolves over time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the discount factor should be used as a dynamic hyper-parameter, and that the learning rate should be adjusted according to the current value of this hyper-parameter.
the discount factor can be a powerful tool to improve deep Q-learning.
we propose a new dynamic strategy for deep reinforcement learning that is able to outperform the standard one in a variety of experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a discount factor in the learning process is crucial to avoid instabilities and to improve the performance of the DQN.
, in order to achieve a good performance, it is important to choose a discount factor that evolves during the learning process.
it is possible, in certain circumstances, to significantly reduce the amount of learning steps required to reach a good performance, without sacrificing the quality of the solution.
